note: A second-class APOSTLE's feast (Bartholomew, Matthew) outranks a per-annum Sunday in the 1955 Tabella, while a second-class martyr's (Lawrence) cedes to it. The grade-level engine treats every second-class feast alike (celebrated over the lesser Sunday), so it matches DO on the apostles but shows Lawrence celebrated where DO commemorates him. Fine per-day-type precedence, deferred.

St Joseph the Worker (1 May, instituted 1955) and the consequent move of Ss. Philip & James to 11 May are calendar changes of 1955 distinct from the Cum nostra rubric reductions; the grade-only derive inherits the 1954 placement. Deferred until the derive carries per-edition placement overrides.

The Dedication of the Archbasilica of the Most Holy Saviour (9 Nov) is graded duplex-ii-classis in the corpus (cited to ordo-1954) but duplex-maius in DO Reduced-1955. A single-feast oracle disagreement on an uncopyrightable grade fact; tracked pending a print cross-check.

Moveable feasts of the Lord the temporal layer does not yet carry (the Commemoration of the Baptism of the Lord, the Holy Name and Holy Family Sundays) and the named Christmastide/post-Epiphany ferias (Title II.14-15). Calendar-level scope; deferred with the temporal engine.

When an early Septuagesima squeezes out a Sunday after the Epiphany, the pre-1955 rite ANTICIPATES that Sunday onto the free Saturday before Septuagesima (DO: 'Dominica VI Post Epiphaniam ~ Semiduplex Dominica anticipata', 13 Feb 1954). The temporal engine does not yet mint an anticipated Sunday, so the Saturday looks free and the Saturday Office of Our Lady (built since #453, correctly ranked below a semidouble) takes it instead of yielding. Rare; deferred to the temporal-engine scope, where an anticipated-Sunday observance will make the lady office yield automatically.
